title: Wrap a gift box with pre-creased paper
instruction: Fold the paper around the gift box, hold the overlapping flaps and secure them with the two tape strips. Leave the wrapped gift on the table and let go.
context: Gift wrapping requires shaping loose material and securing an overlap while keeping it in place. The paper is prepared in advance; cutting and making a bow are outside this task.
setup: A fixed 120 x 160 x 40 mm cardboard gift box rests on the centre of a blue cross-cut sheet of 100 gsm gift paper. Its central rectangle matches the box. The two 120 mm-wide flaps extend 140 mm beyond the long sides; the two 160 mm-wide flaps extend 120 mm beyond the short sides. Each flap is pre-creased 40 mm from its base; its outer panel initially rests about 17 degrees above the table, leaving the edge accessible. Two separate 40 x 12 mm paper-backed adhesive tape strips lie flat to the left of the box, at (22, 14) and (22, 24) cm in the scene’s table coordinates. The box holds the centre of the paper in place. Hands begin open; the setup photograph and scene coordinates fix all positions.
scoring: 1.0 if all four sides and the top are covered, both opposite flap pairs are folded over the top and secured by separate tape strips bridging the upper flap edge with at least 8 mm on each side, and the hands have released the package for three seconds. 0.25 for each secured flap pair, up to 0.5 until the full release condition is met. Otherwise 0. A torn or overextended sheet scores 0. Judge coverage, tape placement and release from video and final photographs; no hidden target or special instrument is required.
fidelity: Native arms and fixed box. Paper uses eight passive hinges with gravity, plastic crease memory, finger-pad and box contact; panels keep their shape between creases. It cannot crumple or form new creases. Tape bonds after flat contact across a folded overlap, then holds that flap pair. The paper centre is fixed. Grasp capture, adhesive traction and feedback forces are simplified.
reset_notes: Reset the paper to its original slightly raised creases and replace the two used tape strips. Restore the fixed starting layout.
